Hello unmarked users,

 

I am fairly new to unmarked so I apologize if the answers to these questions are obvious. I am interested in looking at trends in abundance while accounting for detection probability. I plan on doing this for multiple species but right now I am focusing on Tennessee Warblers. I have five years of data and only one visit per season. I am using dynamics = "trends". messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: population growth rate in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Danielle, what was your maximum value for K?  This should be set to a value higher than is biologically possible.

Your model was structured as an "effects" parameterization, whereby the differences between each year and the baseline year (intercept) are estimated. Therefore, if you want the mean value for a given year, you have to add the intercept to each year's effect estimate.  You could rerun that model with gammaformula= ~year-1 to remove the intercept and get a "means" parameterization, where each estimate is now the mean for the given factor (e.g., year).

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: population growth rate in pcountOpen
parts:
Hi Danielle,

If your data suggest that p was very low, then the model will find it plausible that N was very high, and you will therefore need to set K to a large value. If you do not have robust design data, the model can easily mistake heterogeneity in the abundance dynamics as evidence that p was low.  So try to explain as much of the variation as possible using covariates. If you still have convergence problems, then you probably don't have enough data to estimate the parameters well, and you should consider collecting additional data using the robust design or other sampling methods that provide direct information about the detection process.

It appears as though you coded year as a continuous variable and not a factor. Was that your intention? 

Richard
